settings.appearance.windowTooNarrowForTh: This window is too narrow for three columns, so the list and the message are stacked until you widen it. Your choice is remembered.
settings.tracking.detectionIsFreeBlockin: Detection is free — you can always see that a message tracked you and which company sent the beacon. Premium is what removes it before the request goes out.
settings.tracking.nothingFoundYetScanIsL: Nothing found yet. Messages are scanned as you open them — scanning runs entirely on this device, and no part of an email is sent anywhere.
settings.mailLocation.thisIsTheWorkingCo: This is the working copy — the mail MailVault reads, searches and syncs. By default it lives in the app's own storage. Move it to an external drive or any folder you prefer, and everything follows: messages, headers and attachments.
settings.mailLocation.leavingItThereRedo: Leaving it there means MailVault reads whatever is in its own storage — usually nothing — and re-downloads your mail. The folder you leave behind is not touched.
settings.accounts.removingDeletesEveryth: This removes the account from MailVault. Everything of its in your vault, attachments, and settings for this account will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
settings.storage.ordinaryFilesNothingUpl: Your vault, its attachments, and your settings live on this disk as ordinary files. Nothing is uploaded, and they stay put between sessions.
timeCapsule.browseMailboxAtAnyPointInTim: Browse your mailbox as it was at any point in time. Restore deleted emails with one click. Snapshots are created automatically after each backup.
spellcheck.linuxDictionaryComesFromSyste: On Linux the spelling dictionary comes from your system, not from MailVault, and this machine has none installed. Until one is there, the spellcheck button has nothing to underline.
spellcheck.restartOnceDictionaryInstalle: Restart MailVault once the dictionary is installed — the checker is set up when the app starts.
export.dialog.saveMessageOrThreadOffline: Save a message or a whole thread as an image, or as a single HTML file that keeps working offline. Exporting is a Premium feature.
bugReport.githubThreadIsPublic: A GitHub thread is public. Keep sensitive data out of it, and never upload logs there — logs carry email addresses. If a log would help, send it over email instead.
settings.backup.config.secondCopyActiveP: Second copy active. Plain .eml files, organized by account and folder, readable by any mail app — and untouched if you uninstall MailVault or lose the app's data folder.
settings.backup.config.driveDisconnected: If the drive is disconnected, backups keep running into the app's working copy alone and the second copy catches up — in both directions — the next time the drive is back.
settings.backup.config.oneCopyOnlyChoose: One copy only. Everything lives in the app's data folder — uninstall MailVault, clear app data or lose this Mac and the archive goes with it. Choose an external folder to add a second copy on a drive you control.
settings.backup.config.workingCopyPlusEx: MailVault always keeps its working copy in the app's own storage — that is what you read, search and open in the app. An external folder adds a <0>second, independent copy</0> on a drive you control. It is written at the same time as the working copy, never read by the app day to day, and kept for the long term: emails deleted on the server or in MailVault stay there.
bulk.ops.vaultHoldsSomeUnarchiveIsRisky: Your vault already holds some of these emails, so deleting them from the server is safe. Unarchiving is the risky one: it deletes the vault copy, and anything already gone from the server is then <0>lost for good</0>.
premium.backupSchedule.title: Scheduled automatic backups
premium.backupSchedule.blurb: Daily, weekly or custom schedules per account, with time-of-day control and folder-level checkpoints.
premium.backupHealth.title: Backup health monitoring
premium.backupHealth.blurb: Server, local and external counts per folder, so you can see what is actually safe.
premium.cleanup.title: Email Cleanup
premium.cleanup.blurb: A classifier that learns your mail and sorts it into Newsletter, Promotional, Transactional, Personal, Work and Spam, with keep, archive or delete per category.
premium.timeCapsule.title: Time Capsule
premium.timeCapsule.blurb: Point-in-time snapshots of a mailbox. Browse it as it stood on any earlier date.
premium.trackerBlocking.title: Tracker removal
premium.trackerBlocking.blurb: Strips tracking pixels before a message renders, so senders are never told you opened it. Spotting the tracker is free; removing it is what the subscription adds.
premium.autoCleanup.title: Auto-cleanup rules
premium.autoCleanup.blurb: Archive or delete mail past an age you set, per account and folder, without touching it yourself.
premium.migration.title: Mailbox migration
premium.migration.blurb: Move mail between IMAP accounts with folder mapping and progress you can watch.
premium.serverChange.title: Guided server change
premium.serverChange.blurb: Enter a new host once: IMAP and SMTP are verified, your vault can be uploaded, and a DNS check warns about delivery problems.
premium.exportImage.title: Export as image or HTML
premium.exportImage.blurb: Save a message or a whole thread as a PNG, or as one self-contained HTML file that still reads years later with the network unplugged.
premium.devices.title: Five devices
premium.devices.blurb: One subscription covers up to five installations, managed automatically.
premium.list.title: What Premium includes
